(effective July 1, 2025): https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/cra-arc/formspubs/pub/t4127-jul/t4127-jul-25e.pdf , https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/cra-arc/formspubs/pub/t4127-jul/rates-income-thresholds-constants-25e.csv , https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/cra-arc/formspubs/pub/t4127-jul/other-rates-amounts-25e.csv ; T4127 Jan 2025 CPP/QPP/EI/QPIP tables: https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/cra-arc/formspubs/pub/t4127-jan/cpp-qpp-ttl-01-25e.csv , cpp-qpp-addntl-01-25e.csv , cpp-qpp-scnd-addntl-01-25e.csv , ei-01-25e.csv , qpip-01-25e.csv ; Revenu Quebec income tax rates / principal changes for 2025: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/citizens/income-tax-return/completing-your-income-tax-return/income-tax-rates/ , https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/employers-kit/principal-changes-for-2025-employers-kit/ (Revenu Quebec blocks scripted fetches; QC figures cross-checked via search snippets of those pages).
_notes: Single employee, no dependents, employment income only, full-year resident of one province on Dec 31, 2025. brackets = [lower threshold of taxable income, marginal rate]. Federal lowest rate: legislated cut from 15% to 14% effective July 1, 2025, giving an effective full-year rate of 14.5% for 2025 (used for both the first bracket and all non-refundable credits: BPA, CEA, CPP base contributions, EI premiums). Payroll withholding in Jul-Dec used 14%; annual tax uses 14.5%. From 2026 the rate is 14%. Suggested calc: taxable income = gross - CPP/QPP enhanced contributions (first additional 1% portion + CPP2/QPP2); CPP base credit amount = base portion of contributions (4.95/5.95 of CPP, 5.4/6.4 of QPP). Federal tax = max(0, bracket tax - creditRate*(BPA + CEA + CPP base + EI [+ QPIP])); in QC subtract 16.5% abatement of basic federal tax. Provincial tax similarly with provincial BPA and creditRate, then ON surtax + health premium. Ignored: low-income reductions (ON/BC tax reductions, NS/NL low-income), Canada Workers Benefit, GST/HST and provincial refundable credits, federal 'top-up' credit, provincial CEA except Yukon. Mid-year changes (AB 8% bracket, PE/SK BPA, MB indexation freeze) are given as final full-year 2025 values, not T4127's prorated July payroll figures.

cpp2.notes: On earnings between YMPE 71,300 and YAMPE 81,200; deductible.

ON.healthPremium: Ontario Health Premium on taxable income: $0 up to $20,000; 6% of excess over $20,000 (max $300, reached at $25,000); $300 to $36,000; $300 + 6% of excess over $36,000 (max $450 at $38,500); $450 to $48,000; $450 + 25% of excess over $48,000 (max $600 at $48,600); $600 to $72,000; $600 + 25% of excess over $72,000 (max $750 at $72,600); $750 to $200,000; $750 + 25% of excess over $200,000 (max $900 at $200,600); $900 above.
ON.healthPremiumSegmentsFormat: [incomeThreshold, base, rate, cap]: use the highest segment whose threshold < income; premium = min(base + rate*(income - threshold), cap); 0 if income <= 20,000.
ON.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. Surtax = 20% of (basic ON tax - 5,710) + 36% of (basic ON tax - 7,307), where basic ON tax is after non-refundable credits. Ontario Tax Reduction: basic amount $294 (x2 minus ON tax, floor 0) only matters at low incomes. Ontario Health Premium is added after surtax.

QC.notes: Quebec provincial tax is administered by Revenu Quebec (TP-1), not CRA. Residents pay QPP (payroll.qpp/qpp2) instead of CPP, EI at the reduced Quebec rate (payroll.eiQuebec) and QPIP (payroll.qpip). Federal basic tax is reduced by the 16.5% Quebec abatement (federal.quebecAbatement). Quebec non-refundable credits at 14% (BPA 18,571). Quebec does not grant a provincial non-refundable credit for QPP/EI/QPIP contributions; instead employees get the 'deduction for employment income' (6% of employment income, max about $1,420-1,450 for 2025 - unverified) and QPP enhanced (first additional + QPP2) contributions are deductible. Federal CPP/EI credits apply: federal credit for base QPP portion (5.4/6.4 of QPP), EI (Quebec rate) and QPIP premiums at 14.5% federally. No Quebec health contribution (abolished 2017).

BC.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. BC Tax Reduction: up to $562 for 2025, reduced by 3.56% of net income over about $25,020 (threshold unverified; fully phased out ~ $40,800), so irrelevant for middle incomes.

AB.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. New 8% bracket on the first $60,000 enacted in 2025 and effective for the full 2025 tax year (payroll prorated it as 6% for Jul-Dec to catch up). Non-refundable credits are at 8%; the new Alberta Supplemental Tax Credit tops credits back up to 10% for the portion of total credit amounts exceeding $60,000 (i.e. extra = max(0, credits*0.08 - 4,800) * 0.02/0.08) - irrelevant for a single employee with just BPA + CPP/EI.

SK.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. BPA raised from 18,491 to 19,491 for 2025 (Saskatchewan Affordability Act, +$500/yr planned through 2028 on top of indexing). Payroll used a prorated 19,991 for Jul-Dec; 19,491 is the full-year amount.

MB.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. Manitoba Budget 2025 froze bracket thresholds and BPA at 2024 levels (not indexed) - per T4127 July 2025 (47,000 / 100,000, BPA 15,780). NOTE: CRA's 'last year tax rates (2025)' page lists 47,564 / 101,200 (indexed values); T4127/Budget values used here. BPA phases out for net income between $200,000 and $400,000 (to $0).

NB.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount.

NS.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. Brackets indexed starting 2025. BPA is a flat 11,744 for 2025 (the old income-tested extra $3,000 'BPANS' formula was eliminated).

PE.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. BPA increased from 14,250 to 14,650 effective Jan 1, 2025 (April 2025 budget; payroll prorated 15,050 for Jul-Dec). PEI surtax (10% of PE tax over $12,500) was eliminated starting 2024 - no surtax for 2025.

NL.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount.

YT.notes: Provincial non-refundable credits (BPA, CPP base-contribution credit, EI premium credit) are computed at creditRate (lowest provincial rate). CPP first/second enhanced contributions are deducted from income (not credited). No provincial Canada Employment Amount. Yukon BPA is harmonized with the federal BPA including its phase-out: 16,129 max, reduced linearly to 14,538 for net income between 177,882 and 253,414 (same as federal.basicPersonalAmount). Yukon also has a Canada Employment Amount of 1,471 credited at 6.4%.
